title.narrative: Actions to Combat Climate Threats (ACCT) in Nigeria - CCASE Programme

description.narrative: Majority of the rural population in Nigeria survive through farming activities as agriculture employs 70% of the country’s labour force. Unfortunately, the agricultural sector has severely suffered climate change impacts affecting food production and posing threat to food security. The extreme climatic events such as floods, drought and desertification, have reduced the size of arable lands; greatly affecting agricultural production, a situation that has placed many people, especially women and other vulnerable groups in poverty. Climate change also affects energy resources such as biomass and water resources. The intensive use of biomass as cooking energy for many households, the low access to clean and sustainable energy is hindering effective adaption to the impacts of climate change by rural and vulnerable population. This project aims to build the resilience of women and vulnerable groups in local communities to the impacts of climate change particularly in agriculture and energy sector in FCT, Nasarawa and Benue states of Nigeria. This will be done through promotion of sustainable agricultural practices for improved livelihood opportunities and food security for marginalised groups, facilitating access to sustainable energy for local communities.
